tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: The library closes at ten on weekdays.
guidance: Every chunk must be used exactly once.
Add only the final punctuation.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: Students can borrow up to five books at a time.
guidance: Keep the modal before the main verb.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: The new science building is next to the Student Union.
guidance: The subject is a long noun phrase; keep it together.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
chunks: If you lose your student card
tasks.answer: If you lose your student card, report it to the front desk immediately.
guidance: The if-clause comes first; add a comma before the main clause.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: Although the lecture was difficult, most students found the examples helpful.
guidance: Although introduces a dependent clause; the main clause follows after a comma.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: The university is planning to extend the library's opening hours during the exam period.
guidance: Keep the infinitive phrase after planning.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
chunks: from more than two hundred participants
tasks.answer: Researchers collected data from more than two hundred participants.
guidance: The prepositional phrase modifies data.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: The article argues that social media has changed the way people read news.
guidance: The that-clause is the object of argues.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
chunks: Students who review their notes regularly
tasks.answer: Students who review their notes regularly tend to perform better in exams.
guidance: Keep the relative clause attached to Students.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: The study found a strong connection between sleep quality and academic performance.
guidance: Between ... and ... joins the two noun phrases.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
chunks: If people use public transport more often
tasks.answer: If people use public transport more often, air quality in the city centre will improve.
guidance: The main clause has a future form; the if-clause uses the present.

tasks.prompt: Build one complete, grammatically correct sentence from the chunks below.
tasks.answer: The report recommends that universities provide more support for first-year students who live off campus.
guidance: The relative clause who live off campus modifies first-year students.

tasks.prompt: You are a student representative. Write an email to the university library to request longer opening hours during the exam period. Explain why the change is needed, describe how students are affected, and suggest a specific schedule. Write 100-150 words.
guidance: Use a clear subject line and a polite greeting.
State your request early, then justify it with concrete details.
Close with a specific suggestion and a thank-you.

tasks.prompt: You missed an important group meeting because you were ill. Write an email to your project team. Apologize, explain what happened, ask what you missed, and offer to take on a specific task. Write 100-150 words.
guidance: Apologize briefly and take responsibility.
Ask precise questions about decisions and deadlines.
Offer a concrete contribution rather than a vague promise.

tasks.prompt: You are organizing a campus clean-up event. Write an email to students to invite them. Explain when and where it will take place, what volunteers will do, and how they can sign up. Write 100-150 words.
guidance: Put the key details (date, time, meeting point) in one clear paragraph.
Make the invitation sound welcoming but specific.
Include a clear call to action and a deadline.

tasks.prompt: You rented a bike from a local shop for a week, but the brakes failed on the second day. Write an email to the shop. Describe the problem, explain how it affected your plans, and ask for a refund or a replacement. Write 100-150 words.
guidance: Include the rental dates and any reference number.
Describe the fault factually, without exaggerating.
Make one clear request and set a reasonable deadline.

tasks.prompt: You are applying for a part-time job at the campus café. Write an email to the manager. Introduce yourself, explain any relevant experience, and state when you are available to work. Write 100-150 words.
guidance: Match your experience to the job's customer-service requirements.
Be specific about your weekly availability.
Keep the tone professional and concise.

tasks.prompt: Your student club is organizing a career event. Write an email to a local professional inviting them to speak. Explain the event, why their experience would be valuable to students, and suggest two possible dates. Write 100-150 words.
guidance: Explain the audience and the format of the talk.
Flatter specifically, not generically.
Make responding easy with two date options.

tasks.prompt:
Professor: Some universities require first-year students to live on campus, while others leave the choice to students. What is your view?

Student A: Living on campus saves time and helps students make friends.

Student B: Off-campus housing is often cheaper and gives students more independence.

Write a post responding to the professor's question. Explain your position and refer to the other students' views. Write at least 100 words.
guidance: State your position in the first two sentences.
Engage with at least one classmate's point.
Support your view with a concrete example.

tasks.prompt:
Professor: Should all university students be required to study a foreign language, regardless of their major? Why or why not?

Student A: A foreign language is essential for working in a global economy.

Student B: Students should be free to choose courses that directly support their career goals.

Write a post responding to the professor's question. Explain your position and refer to the other students' views. Write at least 100 words.
guidance: Define what you mean by a requirement.
Address the opportunity cost for students.
Use one specific example from study or work.

tasks.prompt:
Professor: Is online learning as effective as face-to-face instruction for university students?

Student A: Online courses are flexible and let students learn at their own pace.

Student B: Face-to-face classes provide better discussion and accountability.

Write a post responding to the professor's question. Explain your position and refer to the other students' views. Write at least 100 words.
guidance: Separate the mode of delivery from the quality of teaching.
Consider different types of courses.
Give a concrete example of what works or fails online.

tasks.prompt:
Professor: Should universities require students to complete a certain number of volunteer hours before graduating?

Student A: Volunteering builds empathy and connects students to the community.

Student B: Requiring volunteer work turns a genuine activity into a box-ticking exercise.

Write a post responding to the professor's question. Explain your position and refer to the other students' views. Write at least 100 words.
guidance: Distinguish voluntary service from compulsory service.
Address the motivation problem raised by Student B.
Suggest a practical design if you support a requirement.

tasks.topicZh: 作业中的 AI 工具
tasks.prompt:
Professor: Should students be allowed to use AI writing tools for their university assignments?

Student A: AI tools can help students brainstorm and improve their writing.

Student B: Using AI makes it difficult to know what a student has actually learned.

Write a post responding to the professor's question. Explain your position and refer to the other students' views. Write at least 100 words.
guidance: Define acceptable and unacceptable uses.
Discuss how assessment could change.
Give a concrete example of a permitted use.

tasks.prompt:
Professor: Is it better for students to start a career immediately after graduation or to take a gap year first?

Student A: A gap year gives students time to travel, work, and discover what they want.

Student B: Starting immediately keeps momentum and avoids falling behind peers.

Write a post responding to the professor's question. Explain your position and refer to the other students' views. Write at least 100 words.
guidance: Consider financial and family circumstances.
Explain what a productive gap year looks like.
Use a specific example or outcome.
